subject: general
question: The kinetic energy of a moving body of mass 'm' and velocity 'v' is _______.

options.text: directly proportional to its velocity but inversely proportional to its mass
directly proportional to its mass but inversely proportional to its velocity
inversely proportional to its mass and square of its velocity
directly proportional to its mass and square of its velocity

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kinetic energy (KE) of a moving body is given by the formula KE = 0.5 * m * v².
 
• KE is directly proportional to the mass (m) of the body.
 
• KE is directly proportional to the square of the velocity (v²) of the body.
 
• Doubling the mass of the body will double its kinetic energy, keeping velocity constant.
 
• Doubling the velocity of the body will quadruple its kinetic energy, keeping mass constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE):** The energy possessed by an object due to its motion, dependent on mass and velocity.
 
• **Mass (m):** The amount of matter in a body, which directly influences the kinetic energy of the body.
 
• **Velocity (v):** The speed of an object in a particular direction, crucial in determining the kinetic energy as it is squared in the formula.
 
• **Direct Proportionality:** When one quantity increases, the other quantity increases at the same rate. KE is directly proportional to both mass and the square of velocity.
 
• **Energy Conservation:** In a closed system, the total energy remains constant. Kinetic energy can be transformed into other forms of energy but the total energy remains the same.
